standard_prerequisites.name: Idempotent of a ring as a root of t^2 - t
standard_prerequisites.use: Explains why adjoining a root of t^2 - t and inverting t - 1 + x is the right construction and why ebar is a root of the same polynomial modulo I.

standard_prerequisites.name: Quotient of a localisation by an ideal is the localisation of the quotient
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: used at proof lines 1798-1801 to compute A'/IA'
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies A'/IA' with A/I[t]/(t^2 - t) inverted at t - 1 + ebar, which is what makes the required isomorphism visible.

core_obligations: Choose an arbitrary lift x in A of the idempotent ebar and set A' to the ring A[t]/(t^2 - t) with t - 1 + x inverted (proof lines 1792-1794).
Verify that A to A' is etale by computing the derivative 2t - 1 of the relation t^2 - t and noting that (2t - 1)^2 = 1, so that the derivative is invertible in A' (proof lines 1794-1797).

Compute A'/IA' as the quotient polynomial ring A/I[t]/(t^2 - t) inverted at t - 1 + ebar and observe that the map sending t to ebar is an isomorphism, because ebar is a root of t^2 - t (proof lines 1797-1801).
Conclude that the class of t in A' is an idempotent lifting ebar, which is the assertion (proof lines 1801-1803).

difficulty_reason: The lemma is the second of the two lifting examples of the section: given a ring A, an ideal I and an idempotent ebar in A/I, there is an etale ring map A to A' inducing an isomorphism A/I to A'/IA' and carrying an idempotent e' lifting ebar (statement lines 1784-1789). The proof is a 12-line explicit construction (proof lines 1792-1803): it chooses any lift x of ebar, forms the ring A' obtained from A[t]/(t^2 - t) by inverting the element t - 1 + x, checks that A to A' is etale because the derivative 2t - 1 satisfies (2t - 1)^2 = 1 and so is invertible, identifies A'/IA' with A/I[t]/(t^2 - t) inverted at t - 1 + ebar, and shows that the map sending t to ebar is an isomorphism, which also proves that the class of t in A' is an idempotent lifting ebar. The construction of A' and the etale computation are both carried out in full; the only step a reader has to follow is the identification of the quotient of A' by IA' with the quotient of the polynomial ring.
